      "paper_id": "W7220858544",
      "title": "A Semantic-Adaptive Hybrid Retrieval Framework for the Education Domain",
      "authors": "Wei Xiao; K Wang; Aoran Feng; Kunfang Chen; Tai Yu",
      "abstract": "Educational documents, such as textbooks and lecture notes, are characterized by strong logical structure, high contextual dependence, and a high density of technical terms. To address the fragmentation of contextual semantic information and the difficulty of matching key information when large language models (LLMs) are directly applied in the education domain, this paper proposes a semantic-adaptive hybrid retrieval framework for the education domain. First, instead of using traditional fixed-size chunking, the framework designs a dynamic semantic segmentation method based on embedding similarity. This method aims to identify the natural boundaries of knowledge units more accurately and to preserve the integrity of core theorems and principles in long-text derivation. Second, the framework constructs a dual-path hybrid retrieval mechanism that combines BM25-based sparse retrieval with BGE-M3-based dense retrieval, and introduces a Cross-Encoder module for multi-stage re-ranking. This design effectively balances exact matching of domain-specific symbols with the capture of deeper causal semantics. Experimental results show that the proposed framework achieves the best retrieval performance, with an NDCG@10 score of 0.9205. The findings validate the advantages of deterministic semantic segmentation and the proposed retrieval framework in the education domain, and provide an engineering practice paradigm and theoretical basis for building robust domain-specific LLM-based question-answering systems.",

      "paper_id": "W7160574734",
      "title": "Design and implementation of an adaptive hybrid retrieval-augmented generation system for personalized education",
      "authors": "Zhengtao Zhao",
      "abstract": "Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has emerged as a promising approach to im prove factual grounding in large language models (LLMs). However, in educational question answering scenarios with constrained and domain-specific knowledge bases, conventional RAG pipelines still suffer from hallucination, limited retrieval diversity, and insufficient pedagogical adaptability. These issues can significantly undermine the reliability and usability of LLM-based educational systems. This thesis presents an agentic corrective retrieval-augmented generation frame work designed for educational applications. The proposed system integrates hybrid retrieval, query rewriting, document grading, and conditional web-based fallback into an iterative agentic loop, enabling dynamic correction of retrieval and generation fail ures. In addition, a user-profile-driven prompting mechanism is incorporated to adapt response complexity and style to diverse learner needs. Through extensive experiments on curated educational datasets, we empirically demonstrate that the proposed framework significantly reduces hallucination compared to standard RAG baselines, while maintaining retrieval diversity and acceptable re sponse latency. Qualitative analyses further reveal that agentic corrective retrieval is particularly effective in mitigating factual errors arising from incomplete or noisy local knowledge bases. Overall, this work provides practical insights into the design of reliable and adap tive RAG systems for educational settings, highlighting the potential of agentic correc tion mechanisms for safe and effective LLM deployment under knowledge constraints.",

      "abstract": "This study evaluates a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) architecture for higher-education question answering, with particular attention to retrieval quality, answer faithfulness, answer correctness, and the operational behaviour of a multi-tenant deployment.CEREBRO combines dense semantic retrieval and sparse keyword retrieval before response generation by a Large Language Model (LLM).The technical evaluation uses the EduKDQA benchmark and the Retrieval-Augmented Generation Assessment (RAGAS) framework.Three configurations are compared: a non-retrieval baseline, vector-only RAG, and hybrid RAG.Reported Answer Faithfulness scores are 0.42, 0.76, and 0.89, respectively; Answer Correctness scores are 0.38, 0.80, and 0.86.A Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) multi-tenant architecture is also evaluated under simulated workloads of 100, 500, and 1,000 requests per second.Mean Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) increases from 245 ms at 100 requests per second to 462 ms at 1,000 requests per second, while the reported 95th-percentile TTFT at peak load is 495 ms and request success rate is 99.8%.These findings provide a technical evaluation of a hybrid RAG design for institution-specific educational question answering and illustrate the trade-off between retrieval grounding and serving latency in a multi-tenant architecture.",

      "title": "An academic chatbot with hybrid retrieval and local large language models",
      "authors": "Jhon Pa\u00fal Guadalupe Andrade; Blanca Top\u00f3n-Visarrea; Christian Iza",
      "abstract": "Higher-education institutions devote a substantial share of their staff time to answering queries whose answers are already set out in institutional regulations. This paper presents the design and evaluation of an academic chatbot based on retrieval-augmented generation that lets users query those documents in natural language and receive grounded answers in Spanish. The system combines a structure-aware ingestion pipeline, a hybrid retriever that fuses dense semantic search and lexical search through reciprocal rank fusion, and a locally hosted large language model. A distinguishing goal is data sovereignty: every component runs on institutional hardware, so no data is sent to external services. Quality is evaluated with the RAGAS framework over five regulatory documents: the corpus-wide set attains a global score of 0.90, with faithfulness of 0.97. Quality further degrades on long, heavily cross-referenced regulations.       "title": "Hybrid retrieval-augmented generation for hallucination mitigation in domain-specific educational question-answering systems",
      "authors": "Huu Tuong Ho; Lee O-Joun; Duc Tin Ly; Luong Vuong Nguyen",
      "abstract": "Large Language Models (LLMs) offer significant potential for educational chatbots, but their tendency to generate hallucinations and fluent yet factually unsupported responses limits their reliability in high-stakes academic settings. This study presents the design and evaluation of a university-focused virtual assistant, built on a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) architecture, to support academic and administrative inquiries at Greenwich Vietnam. The system integrates a structured institutional knowledge base derived from official documents, internal portals, regulations, and websites, along with hybrid retrieval mechanisms, including lexical and semantic search, query routing, and reranking, to improve evidence selection and contextual grounding. We evaluated the system on a benchmark comprising nearly 700 real-world and expert-constructed question-answer pairs with associated reference sources. Experimental results demonstrate strong retrieval and generation capabilities, achieving a Context Relevance score of 0.92 and a Semantic Answer Similarity score of 0.87, while also receiving high human evaluation scores for accuracy, completeness, freshness, faithfulness, and naturalness. The findings indicate that the proposed RAG-based approach substantially improves the trustworthiness of educational chatbot responses while remaining practical for institutional deployment. At the same time, the study highlights ongoing challenges in handling complex queries and maintaining long-term knowledge freshness, offering useful guidance for future domain-specific RAG systems in higher education.",

      "paper_id": "W7163958414",
      "title": "EduChatQA: curriculum-aware hybrid retrieval and teacher-aligned prompting for textbook-grounded educational QA",
      "authors": "Jingqiang Guan; Jialu Li; Jialu Li; Kun Hou; Jingyuan Li; Jingyuan Li",
      "abstract": "The emergence of large language models (LLMs) has opened new possibilities for education-oriented question-answering (EQA) systems. Nonetheless, limitations in textbook-grounded retrieval, multi-turn discourse control, and response-quality assessment remain pressing challenges. This study presents EduChatQA, a fine-tuned LLM framework that integrates curriculum-aware hybrid retrieval, combining learnable fusion of dense and BM25 signals, with knowledge-graph binding, a role-aligned teacher-student prompt, a dual no-answer head, and a topic-shift detector. A comprehensive evaluation protocol combining classical QA metrics and RAGAS indicators is employed to assess answer quality. Experimental results on the QuAC-Edu benchmark, covering Physics, Chemistry, Biology, and World History, show that EduChatQA achieves an average ROUGE-1 score of 0.69 and a Response Relevancy-5 score of 0.85, outperforming strong baselines by 3\u20136 points in ROUGE-1 and 6\u201310 points in relevancy. Human judgment further reports Context Precision@5 of 0.52, Context Recall of 0.67, and Faithfulness score of 0.71, indicating enhanced grounding in textbook content. Ablation studies on the knowledge graph module show optimal performance with 75\u2013100% triple retention, where Precision@5 reaches 51.6 at full retention. In retrieval-augmented classification tasks, the hybrid retriever achieves a precision of 0.75, recall of 0.76, and F1 score of 0.75, outperforming vector-only and graph-only retrieval strategies. This enhancement is attributable to the symmetric fusion of lexical (BM25) and semantic (dense) signals\u2014an approach that effectively integrates the advantages of each retrieval mode while compensating for their individual limitations. These findings demonstrate that curriculum-aware hybrid retrieval combined with role-aligned prompting provides a reliable, textbook-traceable, and pedagogically coherent solution for classroom-ready EQA systems.",

      "paper_id": "W7126397257",
      "title": "Enhancing Medical Question Answering with LLMs via a Hybrid Retrieval-Augmented Generation Framework",
      "authors": "Bushra Aljohani; Tawfeeq Alsanoosy",
      "abstract": "Given the knowledge-intensive and rapidly expanding nature of medical field, accurately synthesizing and interpreting findings remain a major challenge for clinicians and medical students. Although Large Language Models (LLMs) have advanced automated summarization or generated responses, their deployment is limited by hallucinations, outdated knowledge, and insufficient domain adaptation. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) addresses these issues by grounding LLMs in external knowledge bases. However, as the document corpus scales, maintaining RAG accuracy becomes increasingly difficult, making retrievers critical for contextual relevance. In this paper, we examined the efficiency of a modular RAG framework with a hybrid retrieval strategy that combines sparse retrieval (BM25) and dense retrieval (MedCPT) to extract the most relevant documents from the corpus, thereby providing contextual grounding for the LLM to improve medical responses. Evaluation was conducted on three benchmark healthcare datasets: PubMedQA, MedMCQA, and MedQA-US, using two LLMs, GPT-4o and BioGPT. Performance was assessed using retrieval metrics (context precision, context recall, F1-score) and generation metrics (BERTScore, RAG Assessment Score). The hybrid retriever achieved 92.14% recall, 74.36% precision, and an F1-score of 82.30%. GPT-4o with hybrid retrieval reached 89.4% faithfulness, 82.7% answer relevancy, and an F1BERT of 88.0% on PubMedQA. Results demonstrated that hybrid retrieval within a modular architecture substantially improves retrieval effectiveness and response quality. The proposed work offers a scalable, generalizable solution for high-stakes healthcare applications, supporting flexible retriever integration and robust evaluation to advance transparent QA systems.",
